subject.title: fix(providers): harden Mattermost, Matrix, and Signal

question: Should Crabline unconditionally reject non-loopback HTTP Mattermost endpoints, or preserve existing configurations unless operators opt into strict HTTPS enforcement?
rationale: Rejecting cleartext bearer transport improves credential safety but intentionally stops an existing class of self-hosted configurations, so the permanent compatibility and security policy requires repository-member intent.

options.title: Add Strict Transport Mode
options.body: Preserve existing behavior by default and add an explicit strict-HTTPS option with coverage for compatibility and strict modes.

options.title: Adopt Fail-Closed Upgrade
options.body: Keep the unconditional rejection but document the breaking upgrade behavior and provide focused migration and configuration validation.

options.title: Remove Adapter Enforcement
options.body: Leave TLS enforcement to the deployment and retain the previous acceptance of configured HTTP endpoints.

recommendation.title: Add Strict Transport Mode
recommendation.body: Preserve existing behavior by default and add an explicit strict-HTTPS option with coverage for compatibility and strict modes.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the focused branch implementation and are a repository member positioned to resolve the intended security-versus-compatibility boundary.
